summary: 40-foot wooden DNR live-in lookout built in 1957 above Discovery Bay; sold and taken down by 1971 (Hite dates the decision to 1966); footings reported on the summit.

facts.design: 40-foot wooden live-in tower built for the Washington Department of Natural Resources
facts.status_note: Sold and taken down; the register says gone by 1971 and Hite dates the decision to remove it to 1966; footings reported on the summit

access.note: Summit lies on mixed private timberland and state land; no source says whether the public may enter. Non-motorized use was allowed on Hite's visit

events.note: Built 1957 per the register and Hite; the 1957 open house is reported on the Washington lookouts page
William Muench manned the new station for the remainder of the 1957 season
Mildred Drazkowski named as lookout in 1960 (spelled Milly Draskowski on Hite's page for 1958 to 1960)
Karen Anderson named as lookout for 1966, the last staffing entry in these sources
Hite says a decision was made in 1966 to take the tower down; the tower was sold and parts reused. A US$4 winning bid is reported second-hand from an online source
Register says the tower was gone by 1971, which conflicts with the 1966 removal decision in Hite's account

evidence.supports: built in 1957; 40-foot wooden DNR live-in tower; sold to a private party and parts recycled; gone by 1971
evidence.quote: Built in 1957 and gone by 1971, this 40' wooden DNR live-in tower was sold to a private party and many of the tower parts recycled.

open house; radio and fire finder operating; viewing conditions excellent

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the tower was gone by 1971. Hite says the decision to take it down was made in 1966. The Washington lookouts page gives the sale and removal with no date. The story reports both dates and does not pick one.

resolved_conflicts.field: name of the lookout in 1958 to 1960
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The two pages spell the lookout's name differently: Mildred Drazkowski on the 1960 newspaper quote versus Milly Draskowski on Hite's page. The story uses the newspaper spelling and notes the difference.

notes_for_editor: Removal year conflicts: the register says gone by 1971, Hite dates the removal decision to 1966, and the Washington lookouts page gives no date. The US$4 sale is second-hand from an anonymous online source and is labeled that way. The brief's coordinates and 648 m elevation match the register. Access left as unknown: the summit is mixed private and state land. No photo URLs were captured; Hite's photos are not cited. Brief record was not wrong on status or registration.
